findingMessages.perf-missing-count-restat-on-every-revis: missing_count treats the cache as stale whenever catalog.revision differs, and revision increments on every applied op, including Op::SetDevelop. While a slider is dragged (an op per change) each finished scan is immediately followed by another: the UI thread collects every library photo's path (missing::candidates) and a new worker thread stats every original file. On a 100k-photo library, or one on a network share, this is a continuous stat storm for the whole editing session, duplicating the cached Availability probe the app already has. The documented 'at most every 5 s' bound only applies when the revision is unchanged.
findingMessages.perf-new-smart-album-dialog-queries-ever: The NewSmartAlbum dialog calls catalog.query(&rules, ...) (a full-library filter) and rebuilds filter_label on every frame the dialog is shown, uncached. The Edit smart album dialog uses Caches::rules_view keyed on revision and rules precisely to avoid this. With a large library every pointer move or keystroke while the dialog is open re-scans all photos, making the name field laggy.
findingMessages.perf-rename-keyword-dialog-scans-library: The RenameKeyword dialog scans every photo and every keyword (is_under) each frame just to show a count. Cost is O(photos x keywords) per frame while typing in the field on a large library.
findingMessages.perf-library-caches-flushed-by-every-dev: Every Caches entry (counts, filter_values, date_groups, folder_tree, keyword_tree, people, album counts) is keyed on cat.revision, which Catalog::apply bumps for every op, including Op::SetDevelop applied during slider drags. Panels that are visible then recompute their O(N) library scans per drag step: counts walks all photos, filter_values clones and sorts every camera and lens string, date_groups and trees rebuild. Edits that cannot affect these aggregates still flush them, so editing a photo in a large library costs several full scans per frame.
findingMessages.perf-filmstrip-clones-and-walks-whole-vi: filmstrip() copies the whole visible id list (visible_cloned = visible().to_vec()) and iterates every id each frame to compute a rect and an intersect test, though only about a dozen cells are on screen; the loupe prefetch at line 499 does a second full clone plus a linear position() scan per idle frame. The engine already offers visible_shared (Arc<[PhotoId]> with a generation). At 100k photos this is a per-frame O(N) allocation and walk.
